newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: YPF Q3 net income seen off, operating results up.
newsitem.headline: YPF Q3 net income seen off, operating results up.

text.p: Argentine oil giant YPF SA will announce a third quarter results lower than those of the corresponding 1995 period in terms of net income but clearly higher in operating terms, analysts said.

"We expect a net income of $215 million or $0.61 EPS," said Martin Casa, analyst for Credit Lyonnais Securities. He foresaw an operating result of $400 million against $289 million in third quarter 1995.

YPF, expected to announce its results next week, posted in the third quarter 1995 net income of $264 million ($0.75 EPS), but that included a net extraordinary gain of $65 million. Besides, during that period the company was not paying income taxes due to a loss tax carry-forward.

"In fact, the third quarter 1995's net income would have been $199 million or $0.56 EPS (without the extraordinary gain), which, leaving aside extraordinary results, implies the third quarter 1996 net income is eight percent higher," Cas said.

Andrs Pitchon, head of research at Merchant Bankers, affiliated to Salomon Brothers, said he expected third quarter net income of $229 million ($0.65 EPS) on a record operating income of more than $400 million.
"To appreciate the very positive YPF evolution we must compare operative results and not the net income," he said.
Alejandro Santos, analyst for Bank of Boston, said he expected a net income of $230 million, or $0.65 EPS.

"Results are very good, basically because this year YPF is making provisions for income tax," he said, adding he was expecting better operating results on the back of higher oil prices and better results in its Dallas-based subsidary Maxus.
